name: Sherlock
verdict: No connector path: it is a local, no-auth CLI that checks usernames across sites, with no customer account to connect. The real gate is likely your own privacy and site-terms review.
needGuide: No — nothing to connect; run it in a worker and do your own privacy and site-terms review.

auth.detail: Open-source (MIT) Python CLI that checks a username against 400+ social sites by requesting public profile URLs. No accounts, API keys, OAuth or hosted API. Install with pipx install sherlock-project (or pip, uv, Docker: docker run -it --rm sherlock/sherlock). Options include --json, --csv, --xlsx, --site, --proxy and --timeout (default 60 s).

effort.timeToProduction: Same day if self-hosted; legal review time varies

approval.gate: No approval. The gate is your own compliance review: the tool probes many third-party sites for a person's presence, which raises privacy and site-ToS questions (inference; the README shows no disclaimer).

scopes.summary: None. The tool queries public profile URLs only. NSFW sites are off by default and enabled with --nsfw.

prerequisites: Account and owner: A developer with shell or Docker access runs it; no accounts needed. Run it in your own sandbox or worker, not on customer machines.
Where you register: None needed; install the CLI locally or run the Docker image

registerAt.path: None needed; install the CLI locally or run the Docker image

steps.do: Install with pipx install sherlock-project, or pull the sherlock/sherlock Docker image
Run sherlock <username> --json against a known test username
Wrap the CLI in a worker that restricts inputs, applies timeouts and optional proxies, and parses JSON results
Record the permitted use cases (your own accounts, authorized investigations) in an acceptable-use policy
Add false-positive handling: treat hits as leads that need verification, not identity proof

roles.team: A developer with shell or Docker access runs it; no accounts needed. Run it in your own sandbox or worker, not on customer machines.
roles.customer: None. There is no customer connect flow; end users supply a username as input.

testing: Run sherlock on your own known username and on a throwaway one, using --site to limit scope, --json for parsing and --print-found to reduce noise.

blockers.fix: A hit does not prove the same person. Require human verification before acting.

blockers.problem: Rate-limiting or blocking by target sites
Privacy law (such as GDPR) and site ToS may restrict profiling individuals
blockers.fix: Get legal sign-off and avoid use on private persons without authorization.

blockers.problem: Third-party distro packages (Ubuntu, ParrotOS) may be broken
blockers.fix: Use pipx, uv, pip or Docker.

automation.agentCan: Install and run the CLI, parse JSON/CSV output, build the worker wrapper, and draft acceptable-use and consent wording.
automation.humanMust: Decide legitimate use cases, approve privacy and legal posture, and review results before acting on them.
